content:
Following on from #Physlib > The use of AI in Physlib . I think it might be worth thinking about:

How can we use AI agents to make the review process easier?

Importantly, I am not saying that "we should replace human review with AI review", but I think it is worth thinking about how we can get "AIs to help human reviews". Maybe we should come up with an AGENTREVIEW.md or similar?

I’m not entirely sure, but I think it’s possible to use a GitHub Actions bot to automatically review a PR based on given guidelines. Agents.md should already serve the role of AGENTREVIEW.md; we just need an additional prompt alongside it.

once again, here's a draft PR. I have not tested the GitHub action yet. The main idea is the AGENTS-REVIEW.md casting an agent in the role of a review helper with careful attention to 1) Not pollute the review with low value commentary and 2) Leverage an agent for what it does best in complement to the human reviewer without getting in the way: flag context, concision, topicality (lemmas are scoped to natural theory boundaries), docs, etc. It's basically a Type 1 vs Type 2 thinking division of labor strategy.
Also, I'm not implying that you have to use it. It's just a suggestion that you could build on.

Nice! Will take a look. I think this goes in the direction of @Jinzheng Li 's suggestion of a prompt for the AI-reviewer, (i.e. we don't need to repeat what is in AGENTS.md - just tell the reviewer how to base itself off it).

More generally I was thinking that maybe a general ./Prompts directory would be useful for common tasks we want AI-agents to do in Physlib.

yes, I would only caution though that ./AGENTS.md is rapidly becoming canonical. It's the single, highest value target that anyone's agent basically can't help loading. Since the review agent is instrumented from the repo itself, we can namespace its system prompt wherever it makes sense. As for AGENTS.md, the outward-facing config file, it is conventional to have one at the root of the project, and perhaps more at significant subdirs, ./tests/AGENTS.md, ./docs/AGENTS.md, etc.
